statement: A model M consists of u in R with u >= 0 and r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Its operations are M.mul(a,b)=r(ab) and M.add(a,b)=r(a+b). Trees are finite ordered binary trees built from leaf(a) and node(L,R), with no empty-tree constructor. For arbitrary label types, depth(leaf(a))=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)). For real labels, exactSum(leaf(x))=x and exactSum(node(L,R))=exactSum(L)+exactSum(R). IsPerturbation(B,X,P), for real B and real-labelled trees X,P, means that X and P have identical ordered tree structure and every corresponding pair of leaf labels x,y satisfies |y-x| <= B|x|. This is the relation generated by the supplied leaf and node constructors. For every model M and every tree T with leaf labels in R x R, let d=depth(T). Assume (d+1)u < 1, with the natural number d+1 cast to a real in this inequality. Then there exists a real-labelled tree P such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u),exactProductTree(T),P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(M,T). Here gamma(k,u)=(k u)/(1-k u) for k in N and u in R, casting k to a real. Equivalently, if T has leaves (a_i,b_i), i=1,...,n, then n >= 1 and P has the same ordered shape with leaf labels y_i satisfying |y_i-a_i b_i| <= (((d+1)u)/(1-(d+1)u))|a_i b_i| for every i, and sum_{i=1}^n y_i=roundedDotProduct(M,T). The bound applies to perturbations of exact products, and does not assert perturbations of the two factors separately. The computed scalar first rounds leaf products, then rounds sums recursively according to the supplied tree.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: For every finite ordered binary tree T whose leaf labels are real pairs, returns a real-labelled tree by exactProductTree(leaf((a,b)))=leaf(ab) and exactProductTree(node(L,R))=node(exactProductTree(L),exactProductTree(R)). This is leafwise exact real multiplication, preserving the ordered shape. There is no multiplication or addition at internal nodes.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: A model M consists of u in R with u >= 0 and r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Its operations are M.mul(a,b)=r(ab) and M.add(a,b)=r(a+b). For every model M and finite ordered binary tree T of real pairs, returns a real-labelled tree by roundedProductTree(M,leaf((a,b)))=leaf(M.mul(a,b))=leaf(r(ab)), and roundedProductTree(M,node(L,R))=node(roundedProductTree(M,L),roundedProductTree(M,R)). It rounds each exact leaf product once, preserving the ordered shape and performing no internal-node arithmetic. No depth-dependent inequality is required to define this function.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A model M consists of u in R with u >= 0 and r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Its operations are M.mul(a,b)=r(ab) and M.add(a,b)=r(a+b). For every model M and finite ordered binary tree T of real pairs, returns the real scalar roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,T)). The auxiliary sum obeys roundedSum(M,leaf(x))=x and roundedSum(M,node(L,R))=r(roundedSum(M,L)+roundedSum(M,R)). Thus roundedDotProduct(M,leaf((a,b)))=r(ab), and roundedDotProduct(M,node(L,R))=r(roundedDotProduct(M,L)+roundedDotProduct(M,R)). It rounds each leaf product and each internal-node sum using the given tree; returning a leaf adds no rounding. It does not construct or balance a tree from vectors. No depth-dependent inequality is required for its definition. Under (depth(T)+1)u < 1, the target identifies this scalar with the exact sum of a same-shape perturbation of exactProductTree(T), with the stated relative bound on each product.

assumptions: A model M consists of u in R with u >= 0 and r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Its operations are M.mul(a,b)=r(ab) and M.add(a,b)=r(a+b).
The input tree is arbitrary among finite ordered binary trees of pairs of arbitrary real numbers. No balance, fixed leaf count, sign restriction, or nonzero-label hypothesis is supplied.
The theorem additionally assumes (depth(T)+1)u < 1. Together with u >= 0 and depth(T)+1 >= 1, this makes the gamma denominator positive.

The perturbation condition uses one common bound at every leaf and concerns exact products rather than individual input factors. In particular, an exact product equal to zero must have perturbed label zero.
No particular floating-point format, representable set, or rounding mode is specified beyond the model property; the existential error delta may depend on z.
